metaDescription: Technical architecture of the ISB Security Platform in active development — company-scoped data, shared services and tenant-aware boundaries.
title: Technology designed around operational continuity.
intro: ISB is one platform in active development, with shared services rather than separate applications. Selected offline reporting and patrol workflows are part of the technical foundation. Not every module works offline. Enterprise connectors remain planned.

engineSection.title: Experience, domains, services and foundation.
engineSection.description: Many operational surfaces. One engine underneath. Domains do not recreate identity, audit or storage.

architectureSection.title: Clients, platform services, data and infrastructure.
architectureSection.description: Three layers. Clear boundaries. Shared services above tenant-aware data.

trustNote: Trust architecture — identity, roles, tenant boundaries and audit — continues on Security.

stack.chain: Experience depends on domain · domain depends on services · services rest on foundation
stack.footnote: Many domains. One engine. Domains do not recreate the stack beneath them.

experience.title: Experience layer
experience.purpose: Operational workspaces officers and supervisors actually use.

domain.title: Domain layer
domain.purpose: Operational domains over one shared context — not separate products.

foundation.title: Data / security foundation
foundation.purpose: Tenant isolation, controlled access and integrity concepts.

clients.label: Client experience
clients.detail: Interfaces for officers, supervisors and administrators. Client-facing reporting is in active development. Interface layer only — business logic lives in platform services.

platform.label: Platform services
platform.detail: Shared operational services consumed by every domain. Permissions and tenant context apply before data access.

data.label: Data & infrastructure
data.detail: Operational data and infrastructure controls. Tenant and role context constrain what each client and service may read or write.
items: Selected offline reporting and patrol workflows
